adjudications.source: Original enactment as published: חוק הבחירות לכנסת ולרשויות המקומיות בשנת תש"ל (מימון, הגבלת הוצאות ובקורת), תשכ"ט-1969, Knesset gazette PDF fs.knesset.gov.il/6/law/6_lsr_208008.PDF, read from the Internet Archive capture of 12 March 2023 (https://web.archive.org/web/20230312184944id_/https://fs.knesset.gov.il//6/law/6_lsr_208008.PDF), §§1–2 and the two Schedules; explanatory notes (ה"ח 807, p. 54) unreachable.
adjudications.support: לכל המפלגות המנויות בתוספת הראשונה יוקצב מאוצר המדינה סכום כולל של 14,400,000 לירות למימון הוצאות הבחירות — First Schedule: every faction of the outgoing Knesset, coalition and opposition (Alignment 7,440,000 down to seven single-seat lists at 120,000 each, among them Rakah, Haolam Hazeh and MK D. Ben-Gurion); Second Schedule: Free Centre 480,000.
adjudications.reason: Coder B's No is adopted and now rests on the published text rather than on the committee chair's summary: the beneficiaries are all factions of the outgoing Knesset at a uniform 120,000 lirot per seat, government and opposition alike, and MK Ben-Gurion appears by name only to receive the same per-seat sum as other single-seat lists, so no specific interest of the sitting government or of an identified officeholder is addressed; Coder A left the cell blank only because the text was unreachable.

adjudications.source: Divrei HaKnesset, 6th Knesset, NYU Faculty Digital Archive mirror: sitting 366 of 22 Jan 1969 with the agenda and the summary of sittings 364–366 (https://archive.nyu.edu/handle/2451/71327, pp. 42–43); 18 Feb 1969 (https://archive.nyu.edu/handle/2451/71300, p. 1); 19 Feb 1969 (https://archive.nyu.edu/handle/2451/71293, pp. 36–46); gazette footnote in 6_lsr_208008.PDF.
adjudications.support: Agenda for sittings 364–366 (20–22 Jan 1969), item כא: the financing bill '(קריאה ראשונה) – הצעת קבוצת חברי כנסת'; the summary of those sittings records no first reading; 18 Feb: הונח לקריאה שנייה ושלישית ... שחזר מוועדה משותפת; third reading passed 19 Feb; gazette: נתקבל בכנסת ביום א' באדר תשכ"ט (19 בפברואר 1969).
adjudications.reason: Coder B's Yes is verified: the bill still awaited its first reading at the 20–22 January sittings and was tabled for second and third reading on 18 February, so the final vote of 19 February came at most 27 days (30 on the most generous reading) after the first reading, within the sheet's thirty days; Coder A's blank reflected only that A had not located these sittings in the mirror (A's cited Knesset PDF 6_lsr_208007 is in fact the July 1969 amending law, not the original).

adjudications.source: Original enactment text (6_lsr_208008.PDF via the Internet Archive, as above), §§2–4, 7–9, 11–13.
adjudications.support: לא תוציא מפלגה להוצאות בחירות סכום העולה על סך-כל המורכב משנים אלה ... מבקר המדינה יבקר את מערכת החשבונות האמורה בסעיף 9
adjudications.reason: Coder B's No stands on the published text: the law grants treasury financing to the scheduled factions, caps their election spending at the grant plus one third, funds voter transport through the Central Elections Committee and conditions the final 30% on a State Comptroller audit, so it adds a funding entitlement and an audit and removes no check on the government and no protected right, and the sheet's scope definition is not met; Coder A's blank was for want of the text.

adjudications.source: Original enactment text (6_lsr_208008.PDF via the Internet Archive, as above), §1 (definition of מפלגה and בחירות), §2(א)–(ב), §3 and the Schedules; Divrei HaKnesset 19 Feb 1969 (2451/71293, p. 36) for the committee chair's statement of the allocation principle.
adjudications.support: 'מפלגה' – מפלגה ששמה נקוב בתוספת הראשונה או בתוספת השניה — Schedules allocate 120,000 lirot per seat of the outgoing Knesset; Kargman: חלוקת ההקצבות על חשבון המדינה תהיה לפי תוצאות הבחירות לכנסת השישית.
adjudications.reason: Coder B's Limited is adopted: the text confines state election financing to the factions named in the Schedules in proportion to the previous Knesset's results and, by its definition of מפלגה, leaves any new list outside the scheme altogether, which engages free and equal elections (the principal value) and contradicts it to a limited extent, since it is a single-election measure counterbalanced by an expense cap and a Comptroller audit (rule of law, entrenched), and contradiction takes precedence over entrenchment; Coder A's blank was for want of the text.

adjudications.source: Divrei HaKnesset, 6th Knesset, sitting 424 of 8 July 1969 (https://archive.nyu.edu/handle/2451/71270, p. 1) and 15 July 1969 (https://archive.nyu.edu/handle/2451/71299, pp. 81–85), NYU Faculty Digital Archive mirror.
adjudications.support: 8 July: הונחו היום על שולחן הכנסת, לקריאה ראשונה, מטעם הממשלה: ... 2. חוק הבחירות (אישור תקפם של חוקים), תשכ"ט-1969; 15 July: Unna: החוק חזר מהוועדה בשינויים אלה, then the third-reading vote.
adjudications.reason: Coder B's Yes is verified in the record: the government bill was tabled for first reading on 8 July 1969 and passed its third reading on 15 July 1969, so the final vote came at most seven days after the first reading; Coder A's blank reflected only an unsuccessful search of the mirror.

adjudications.source: Divrei HaKnesset, 15 July 1969 (https://archive.nyu.edu/handle/2451/71299, p. 85), NYU Faculty Digital Archive mirror.
adjudications.support: הצבעה: בעד החוק – 68, נגד – 8, נמנעים – 5. חוק הבחירות (אישור תקפם של חוקים), תשכ"ט-1969, נתקבל.
adjudications.reason: Coder B's tally is confirmed verbatim in the Knesset record of the third reading, and 68 votes in favor exceed the sixty-one the variable requires; Coder A had found no tally.

adjudications.source: Hebrew Wikisource, חוק-יסוד: חופש העיסוק (https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק-יסוד:_חופש_העיסוק), §8(א) (ס"ח תשנ"ד 90; the 1998 amendment altered only the closing words and added §8(ב)).
adjudications.support: הוראת חוק הפוגעת בחופש העיסוק תהיה תקפה אף כשאינה בהתאם לסעיף 4, אם נכללה בחוק שנתקבל ברוב של חברי הכנסת ונאמר בו במפורש
adjudications.reason: Coder A's No is adopted because the variable turns on the enactment's subject and the override clause's subject is the validity of statutes infringing the right under stated legislative conditions (a Knesset majority, an express statement, a four-year expiry), naming no court, review, appointment or tenure; Coder B's 'immunity from judicial invalidation' is an inferred effect that the sheet captures under direction (where both coders agree on Illiberal) rather than under this variable, and the same reading gave both coders No for the limitation clause of enactment 1.

adjudications.source: חוק-יסוד: הממשלה (תיקון מס' 12), ספר החוקים 3031, 27 March 2023, pp. 72–73, Knesset gazette PDF fs.knesset.gov.il/25/law/25_lsr_2117656.pdf read from the Internet Archive capture of 26 January 2024 (https://web.archive.org/web/20240126222111id_/https://fs.knesset.gov.il/25/law/25_lsr_2117656.pdf); cross-checked against the Nevo consolidated text (https://www.nevo.co.il/law_html/law00/73690.htm) and the Wikisource wikitext (https://he.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=חוק-יסוד:_הממשלה&action=raw).
adjudications.support: Sole section 'תיקון סעיף 16 – 1. בחוק-יסוד: הממשלה, בסעיף 16, אחרי סעיף קטן (ב) יבוא: (ב1)...', then the footnote התקבל בכנסת ביום א' בניסן התשפ"ג (23 במרץ 2023) and the signatures; the words תחילה/תחולה do not occur.
adjudications.reason: Coder B's Yes is confirmed on the gazette text itself, basis 'by absence of a clause': the published amendment consists of one amending section with no commencement or deferral provision, and the label '(החל מתחילת כהונתה של הכנסת העשרים ושש)' that troubled Coder A is a Wikisource editorial note (template ח:הערה) absent from the published text and from Nevo, so the cell is settled without reading any court material.

adjudications.source: Press reports of the recorded tally: Times of Israel 23 Mar 2023 (https://www.timesofisrael.com/knesset-passes-law-shielding-netanyahu-from-recusal-in-61-47-final-vote/), Jerusalem Post (https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/politics-and-diplomacy/article-735156), Kipa (https://www.kipa.co.il/חדשות/1154150-0), Walla (https://www.walla.co.il/news/politics/3567511), JDN (https://www.jdn.co.il/news/politics/1934105/); Knesset vote tables in the sheet's extract end 13 July 2021; Knesset OData geo-blocked.
adjudications.support: Tally 61 for, 47 against, about 6 a.m. 23 March 2023; absentees reported: Bitan and Amsalem (Likud), Abutbul (Shas), Abbas (Ra'am), and per Walla Edelstein (Likud); no report gives a faction breakdown or states that no opposition MK voted for.
adjudications.reason: Coder B's blank is adopted: the sheet permits Yes only where the record shows no opposition member voting for and requires a blank where the vote record is unavailable, and here the press gives only the tally with conflicting lists of absentees, so Coder A's arithmetic (64 coalition seats less three named absentees equals 61) is an inference the sheet forbids and is not even stable across reports (Walla's fourth coalition absentee would leave 60).

adjudications.source: Gazette text of §16(ב1) (ספר החוקים 3031, pp. 72–73, via the Internet Archive copy above); identical wording on Nevo and Wikisource.
adjudications.support: ותיקבע באחד משני אלה בלבד ... וועדת הכנסת אישרה את הודעתו ברוב של שני שלישים מחבריה ... הממשלה החליטה, ברוב של שלושה רבעים מחבריה
adjudications.reason: Coder A's No is adopted because the check at issue, a determination that the prime minister is incapacitated, is not removed but redefined, and the text itself supplies the mechanisms (the prime minister's own notice or a three-quarters cabinet decision, each approved by two-thirds of the Knesset Committee, with extensions by eighty MKs and termination by the Committee), so the definition's condition that no alternative mechanism exist is not met; Coder B's Yes presupposes a pre-existing check, incapacity on non-health grounds declared by an actor outside those routes, that the unamended §16(ב) does not state, and establishing it would need sources the sheet forbids.

adjudications.source: Gazette text of §16(ב1) (as above); explanatory notes as quoted in the coders' press sources (JDN 13 Mar 2023, ICE 23 Mar 2023, Times of Israel 1 Mar 2023; not re-fetched); Walla 23 Mar 2023 (https://www.walla.co.il/news/politics/3567511) on the final text.
adjudications.support: Walla: הסעיף המתייחס לביטול הביקורת השיפוטית על תהליך היציאה לנבצרות של ראש הממשלה הורד מנוסח החוק — the enacted text names no court, and the notes as quoted speak only of ביטול תוצאות הבחירות וההליך הדמוקרטי.
adjudications.reason: Coder A's Neutral is adopted: the enacted text and the explanatory notes as quoted engage none of the three axes, naming no court, no judicial review and no identity, minority or women's matter, and the clause barring judicial review that press reports describe in the bill was dropped before passage, so the principal subject is a procedural rule on the organs, grounds and majorities for determining incapacity; Coder B's Illiberal reads 'בלבד' as narrowing judicial determination, which the text does not say and which the sheet's bar on inference excludes (B's reading is recorded as the alternative, and the agreed deviation_tier Limited already captures the narrowing of accountability under rule of law and separation of powers).

deviations: Knesset hosts were geo-blocked for the adjudicator as for the coders (fs.knesset.gov.il returned an 'Unavailable' HTML page; knesset.gov.il/Odata redirected to maintenance-page-geo). In their place I read Internet Archive (web.archive.org) captures of the Knesset's own gazette PDFs: 25_lsr_2117656.pdf (capture 26 Jan 2024) for enactment 8, and 6_lsr_208008.PDF (capture 12 Mar 2023) for the original February 1969 text of enactment 2. These are copies of the gazette text and are used on the same footing as the Wikisource and Nevo copies the sheet names. The archive was intermittently offline during the session.

The Knesset PDF Coder A cited for enactment 2 (6_lsr_208007.PDF) is, on reading the archived copy, the July 1969 amending law (financing for new lists), not the original enactment; it was downloaded, identified and not used for coding. The original's explanatory notes (ה"ח 807, p. 54) remain unreachable; named_beneficiary is therefore coded from the text alone.

Knesset records used are the NYU Faculty Digital Archive's Divrei HaKnesset PDFs (handles 2451/71327, 71300, 71293, 71270, 71299), which do carry a text layer; text was extracted locally with pypdf, which scrambles word order within lines, so quotations were reassembled from the visible words and should be checked against the PDFs. Coder A's statements that the mirror holds no 18–19 February 1969 and no July 1969 sittings were wrong; the handles Coder B cited exist and contain what B reported.

Search-result snippets exposed litigation material: Israel Democracy Institute and Kohelet pages on the incapacity amendment with a High Court case number, an IDI op-ed, a court-judgment PDF hosted at netanya.ac.il returned for the enactment 2 search, and a snippet about a hearing on deferral of the amendment. None of those pages was opened and nothing from the snippets was used. The JDN article's related-link headline on the law's effective date concerned a court ruling and was disregarded. The Hebrew Wikisource page for Basic Law: The Government lists a court case in its header and in the tag on §16; I used only the statutory text and the page markup (which shows the deferral label as a ח:הערה editorial note) and did not open the case link. Kipa 1173669, which Coder B identified as a ruling, was not opened.

Enactment 8 vote record: the Kan report (kan.org.il 218893) returned 403 and was not read; the Knesset OData vote tables are geo-blocked; no mirror of the 23 March 2023 roll call was found; the coalition_only cell is left blank on the tally and the conflicting absentee reports alone. The explanatory notes of enactment 8 (ה"ח הכנסת 952, 13 Mar 2023, p. 52, as the gazette footnote cites them) were not reachable; they are relied on only as quoted in the coders' press sources, which both coders used for the agreed named_beneficiary cell.

Not found: the exact first-reading dates of enactment 2 (bounded to 23 January–17 February 1969 by the sittings agenda, the sittings summary and the 18 February tabling) and of enactment 3 (bounded to 8–14 July 1969 by the tabling and the committee's return of the bill); neither affects the expedited coding.

No file in the sheet's folder other than coding-sheet.md, coder-A.json and coder-B.json was opened, listed or searched. The session scratchpad contained files from earlier work (including one named bergman.txt), which were not opened; every download was placed in a fresh subdirectory (scratchpad/adj/...) and read only with an isolated Python interpreter.
